sanitized_brief: UK Parliament Hackathon with EasyA is an in-person event at the House of Commons on 2026-09-04, 12:30-17:30. The operator-supplied deadline is 2026-09-04. Evidence says participants may start building from 2026-08-24, so this is roughly an 11-day build window ending in a pitch day rather than a same-day code sprint. Maximum team size is 5. Projects must have AI and/or crypto/blockchain as a core mechanism; no specific model, chain, SDK, dataset, or repository format is mandated in the supplied evidence. The audience includes UK government decision-makers such as MPs, Lords, and civil servants, plus EasyA's Web3/developer community. Required presentation evidence is a pitch on 2026-09-04; the supplied organiser summary says a working demo understandable to non-technical parliamentarians in a few minutes matters more than a slide-only vision. No formal judging rubric, tracks, exact prize amounts, or artifact checklist are published in the supplied material. Implied criteria are AI/crypto substance, parliamentary relevance, and demo clarity, but no weights should be invented. Prizes mentioned are equity-free prize money, follow-on grants, job/internship opportunities, and a special non-coder prize. Useful capabilities include EasyA's Web3 community, workshops, and access to policymakers, startups, recruiters, VCs, and potential grant pathways. Crowding labels: avoid generic chatbot wrappers, plain document/PDF summarizers, dashboard-only analytics, recommendation lists without last-mile action, and slide-only visions. Potentially underexplored directions include appeal-pathway reconstruction, constraint-based resource allocation under official rules, administrative error prevention, eligibility inconsistency detection across agencies, procedural fairness/case-queue simulation, and failure-surface minimisation for demonstrations.
